statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 9% while Stress is extreme at 81%.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. The extreme Stress reading reflects 52-week-high long-end Treasury yields, Brent above $100 on the unresolved US-Iran conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, and a high-impact PPI print inside the next 24 hours rather than any observed no-retracement price path. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged around the 12:30 UTC PPI release and the US cash open on 10 September; outside it, conditions are described as orderly and two-sided.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes modestly lower as long-end yields set 52-week highs and Brent tops $100; overnight futures quiet and two-sided
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,421.55, down 0.29%, inside a 29,334.40-29,563.60 session range of roughly 0.78%. The decline was shallow at index level but broad beneath it: the Dow fell about 0.77% and the Russell 2000 about 1.30%, and seven of eight tracked megacaps were lower in the latest session, with the index cushioned mainly by Meta's 6.55% advance on its Muse AI agent launch. Semiconductors were a constructive offset, with AMD, MU, QCOM and INTC all higher. The clearest stress channel was rates: the 10-year closed at 4.837% after tagging a 52-week high of 4.857%, and the 30-year sat near 5.28%. Crude extended sharply, with WTI near $97 and Brent above $101, as US and Iranian forces continued tit-for-tat strikes on tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz; 42 tankers were reported waiting to transit. VIX rose 4.7% to 16.46, still low in absolute terms. Delayed cross-asset context was mixed rather than aligned, with index futures flat to slightly higher, VIX futures lower, crude higher and Treasury futures near unchanged. Against that backdrop, current NQ price-path evidence is the decisive input: after the cash close, futures traded near 29,426, about 0.1% lower, inside a narrow 29,416.25-29,472.75 band on light volume. That is two-sided, orderly repricing with no directional efficiency, no shallow-pullback sequence and no session-extreme holding, which is why Tail is held low even though the amplifier stack, elevated long yields, a crude discontinuity risk and weak breadth, is genuinely present. The next 24 hours contain August PPI and weekly jobless claims at 12:30 UTC and existing home sales at 14:00 UTC on 10 September, with the US cash open at 13:30 UTC falling between them; August CPI follows on 11 September and the FOMC decision with projections on 16 September.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the preceding 24 clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 09:00-10:00 UTC slot on 9 September has none and is marked unavailable. Tail sat between 7% and 9% through the Asian and European overnight, rose into the European and pre-US session to a 20% peak in the 12:00 UTC hour, the only yellow WATCH slot in the window, then decayed steadily through the US cash session to 9% by 22:00 UTC as price discovery stayed orderly. Stress climbed monotonically from 73% to a 83% peak and settled at 81%, reflecting the rates and crude backdrop rather than index path damage. Confidence held in a tight 87-89% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 9-13% band through the Asian and European overnight, where the main mechanism is headline discontinuity from the Strait of Hormuz into thinner liquidity rather than trend persistence. Tail then steps up into the 12:30 UTC PPI window on 10 September and peaks at 20%, mapping to WATCH, in the 13:00 UTC hour where the post-release repricing overlaps the US cash open. It decays back toward the overnight baseline through the US afternoon, with a smaller lift into the power hour before the 20:00 UTC close. Stress stays extreme throughout, peaking at 86% in the cash-open hour, and Confidence declines gradually from 88% to 79% as each slot moves further from verified live evidence.
